headline: Revenue grows; margins compress; last year's charge fades
summary_short: Revenue was $403.6M, up 8.5% y/y (down 2.2% q/q), while net income of $57.1M reversed a $170.7M year-ago loss that had included a $217.9M after-tax discontinued-operations writedown on the now-divested Sound United business.
summary_long: Revenue rose 8.5% y/y to $403.6M on higher consumables/service sales and a ~$5.6M FX tailwind; direct/distribution sales grew 10.2% while OEM revenue fell 5.2%. Gross margin compressed to 62.1% from 62.9% on $6.7M of incremental tariffs, partly offset by cost efficiencies. SG&A rose 20.1% on $17.9M of costs tied to the pending Danaher acquisition ($180.00/share cash, stockholder-approved May 1, 2026); R&D fell 11.5% on lower compensation. Net income of $57.1M reversed a $170.7M year-ago loss, which included a $217.9M after-tax writedown when the now-divested Sound United business was classified held-for-sale. No forward guidance was issued in the filing. Capex was $5.3M; no share repurchases.

drivers.explanation: Grew on higher consumables and service sales plus a ~$5.6M FX tailwind. Direct/distribution sales +10.2% to $365.0M; OEM revenue -5.2% to $38.6M.
COGS rose $14.8M on higher sales volumes and $6.7M of incremental tariffs, partly offset by operational efficiencies; gross margin fell to 62.1% from 62.9%.
SG&A rose 20.1% on $17.9M of Danaher-merger transaction costs plus higher compensation; R&D fell 11.5% on lower compensation, partly offset by engineering project costs.
Prior-year quarter absorbed a $217.9M after-tax discontinued-operations writedown (Sound United held-for-sale); that business is now fully divested, so no comparable charge recurred.
Masimo agreed Feb 16, 2026 to be acquired by Danaher for $180.00/share cash; stockholders approved the merger May 1, 2026, with closing subject to regulatory approval.
